rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing the simplest configuration (rna_only with PCA encoder and singleprofile). This clarifies the performance of a minimal model, providing a reference point to evaluate more complex designs later. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder and profile setting, addressing foundational design choices before exploring multimodal or advanced aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same RNA encoder but avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (using a proven RNA encoder), providing clarity on whether multiprofile or aggregation methods improve performance.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with avgpool aggregation. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation improves performance in the same multiprofile setup, isolating the effect of aggregation. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice (aggregation method) with minimal parameter changes, providing clarity on whether more complex aggregation improves results.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) maintains or improves performance in the multiprofile/avgpool setup. This clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, while keeping other factors constant. It balances exploration (testing a better encoder) and exploitation (building on the multiprofile/avgpool success).

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005, 0.650 accuracy) is highly effective. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) further improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It directly builds on the strongest current direction while exploring a key design choice with minimal additional changes.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 RNA encoder achieve higher accuracy (0.65) than singleprofile. This experiment tests singleprofile with scvi_n200 to isolate the impact of profile setting, clarifying whether multiprofile is a critical factor. It balances exploration (testing profile settings) and exploitation (using scvi_n200, a high-performing encoder).

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (config_002, 005, 006) outperform singleprofile, and scvi_n200 (config_005, 006) is better than pca_n2000. However, scgpt (config_008) has not been tested. This experiment tests scgpt in multiprofile with avgpool, isolating the RNA encoder's impact. It balances exploration (testing a new encoder) and exploitation (using multiprofile, which is proven effective).

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and multiprofile achieve high accuracy (0.65). However, scgpt (RNA encoder) has not been tested in singleprofile settings. This experiment tests scgpt with singleprofile to isolate its performance relative to scvi_n200, addressing uncertainty about encoder choice and profile setting impact. It balances exploration of new encoders while building on existing high-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile and scvi_n200 RNA encoders outperform others. This experiment tests image-only models with multiprofile and the high-performing imagenet_vit_l image encoder, isolating the impact of image data. It balances exploration of image modality against RNA-only strengths, addressing uncertainty about image data's contribution to performance.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve high accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder using transformer aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It directly builds on the strongest RNA-only baseline while testing a critical design choice (multimodal fusion) with minimal additional complexity.
